# ASMR sound effects

**Current status: this folder is populated with synthetic placeholder sounds**, generated by
`scripts/tools/generate_placeholder_sfx.py` using only ffmpeg's built-in noise/filter
synthesis (filtered pink/white/brown noise + tremolo, loudness-normalized). They're 100%
original/no licensing concerns, and good enough to have real sound in the pipeline immediately,
but they're an approximation, not real field recordings — chopping/footsteps/utensil sounds in
particular are rhythmic filtered noise, not the real thing. Swap any of them out any time by
dropping a real recording in with the same filename (see sourcing options below); nothing else
needs to change.

Re-run `python scripts/tools/generate_placeholder_sfx.py` any time to regenerate/retune them
(edit the RECIPES dict in that file to change a tag's texture).

## Original instructions (for replacing placeholders with real recordings)

`assemble_video.py` looks for a file named `<tag>.mp3` in this folder for each audio tag the
day's story uses. If a file is missing it silently falls back to silence for that scene and
prints a warning — the pipeline still runs, it just won't have that sound.

Add mp3 files with these exact names (loopable, a few seconds to ~30s each is enough since
they get looped/trimmed to each scene's length):

```
rain.mp3
birds.mp3
river.mp3
wind_leaves.mp3
footsteps_wet_soil.mp3
chopping.mp3
grinding_stone.mp3
water_pouring.mp3
rice_washing.mp3
dough_kneading.mp3
oil_sizzling.mp3
clay_pot_boiling.mp3
wooden_spoon_stirring.mp3
fire_crackling.mp3
utensil_clinks.mp3
banana_leaf.mp3
steam.mp3
eating_ambience.mp3
```

## Where to get them for free

These are one-time manual downloads (not something to automate/scrape) — check each clip's
license before use:

- https://freesound.org — huge library, many CC0 (no attribution needed) clips; filter by
  license.
- https://pixabay.com/sound-effects/ — royalty-free, no attribution required.
- https://mixkit.co/free-sound-effects/ — free for any use, no attribution required.

Search each site for the tag name (e.g. "rain loop", "chopping vegetables", "fire crackling")
and drop the downloaded file into this folder with the matching name above.
